column1: # The same contract as pipeline_cases.tsv, against the Romanian pack.
# Its own file because the language is the fixture: a word is correct or not only with respect
# to a dictionary, and "in" means opposite things in the two. Romanian is also where most of
# this keyboard's reports come from.
#   typed <TAB> committed <TAB> situation
# Every line here is a requirement: what the keyboard must do, not what it currently does.
# Three of these once described a defect and were written green so the suite would pass. That
# was a mistake worth naming, because it inverts what a suite is for: a passing line is
# indistinguishable from a requirement, so CI went green *enforcing* the bug, and no change to
# the keyboard was ever going to turn it red. A defect belongs in the tracker or in a red test,
# never in a green one.
totusi
# "daca" must reach "dacă" (94,655). The name "Dacia" entered the pack with the entity-name
# merge on 2026-09-20 and outranks it; the proper-noun guard then refuses the name, so nothing
# is committed and the accent is never restored. A name outranking an ordinary word by a factor
# of a hundred is the trade the names list was never meant to make.
daca
# "in" must reach "în" (1,782,296) -- the commonest word in the language, and the plainest case
# the accent restoration exists for. The diacritic-free spelling folds onto the accented one
# exactly, so it is reached at no cost at all, and a zero-cost endpoint is scored as merely
# unpenalised rather than as the strong reading it is. "ins" (508) is offered instead.
in
snobul
# "cana" must reach "cană" (170) and not "canal" (1,369). Both are reachable from the letters
# typed: the first is the typed word with its diacritic restored, the second a different word
# with a letter added. Ranked on frequency alone the commoner one wins -- which is the whole
# defect, and why "totusi" -> "totuși" (9,779) has always worked while this never did. Not two
# behaviours; one rule, decided by whichever side happens to be commoner.
cana
